diagrams.reason: C1 (When does an @name join a section instead of remaining prose or routing a task?): Rejected: existing Figure 1 and the §4.2 examples already show every routing branch. C2 (Why choose named sections over the alternative approaches?): Rejected: alternatives and disagreements are comparisons fully expressed by existing tables, not a flow. C3 (What must change so # headings are not lost or mistaken for pages?): Rejected: §2 facts and Phase 0 already give the two parser corrections; a drawing would merely restate the short list. C4 (What happens to duplicate, reserved, or escaped declarations?): Rejected: §4.1 short lists already give all declaration acceptance, merge, and ignore conditions. C5 (Which annotation's tag controls a combined underline or continuation block?): Rejected: the head → followers → absorbed-underlines priority is a short ordered rule; no new spatial relationship. C6 (Which component owns section membership and which components only render it?): Rejected: existing Figure 2 already shows source ownership, managed-region projection, JSON, and viewers. C7 (How does a page-ordered note become a section-ordered note while preserving independent quote cards?): Rejected: the worked Markdown example and hierarchy bullet already show section → page → independent member structure and the legacy fallback. C8 (How does the region parser distinguish a section title from a page label?): Rejected: §4.6 compact list already specifies the complete card-signature branch, H3/H4 interpretation, and legacy fallback. C9 (Why must positional tag tokens be ignored on both sides of ID matching, even after declaration deletion?): Rejected: §4.7 rule 1 and its three sub-bullets already enumerate both-sided stripping and both failure cases; before/after boxes would repeat them. C10 (How do old Mac and Linux readers degrade when a sectioned note arrives?): Rejected: the explicit version-mismatch and old-reader bullets already enumerate the outcomes; a diagram would only redistribute those cases. C11 (Where do sections appear, and how are unresolved tags exposed?): Rejected: the surface table and diagnostic list already provide the mapping, while Figure 1 covers tag failures. C12 (What happens if Highlights does not export the declaration syntax unchanged?): Rejected: one conditional sentence gives the only branch—if export changes #, choose another spelling before building. C13 (What must be verified and delivered before the Mac panel and later polish?): Rejected: the numbered phase plan already presents the gates and delivery order; this would be a short linear chain. C14 (Which evidence supports the recommendation?): Rejected: the bibliography supplies evidence references, not an ordered, conditional, or causal mechanism.
